short: A series of devastating Russian naval raids along the Swedish coast aimed at forcing peace negotiations.
full:
Between 1719 and 1721, the Russian galley fleet launched extensive raids along the eastern coast of Sweden, including the Stockholm archipelago. Utilizing their shallow-draft galleys, Russian forces bypassed heavier Swedish warships to land troops, burn towns, destroy ironworks, and pillage estates. The campaign was intended to terrorize the population and coerce the Swedish government into accepting Russian peace terms.

The raids caused massive economic destruction and demonstrated Sweden's inability to defend its own heartland. The relentless pressure finally succeeded in breaking Swedish resolve, directly leading to the signing of the Treaty of Nystad in 1721 and the conclusion of the Great Northern War.
